analysis.evidence: וְעַתָּה introduces the verdict אָרוּר אָתָּה, “you are cursed.” It marks the curse as the consequence of Cain’s shedding his brother’s blood, which the ground received from his hand.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to the adverb עַתָּה.

draft.change: Add a Hebrew root article for ארר with the Qal verb אָרַר and its passive participle אָרוּר.
draft.definition: To pronounce a curse on someone. The passive participle describes the one under the curse.
draft.evidence: In Gen.3.14 Yahweh pronounces the serpent cursed for what it has done and declares how it will live.

analysis.evidence: In אָרוּר אָתָּה (“you are cursed”), the masculine singular participle agrees with אָתָּה. Yahweh pronounces the curse on Cain, whose brother’s blood the ground received from his hand.
analysis.morphology: Qal passive participle, masculine singular absolute, used predicatively.
analysis.sense: To pronounce a curse on someone.

analysis.evidence: In אָרוּר אָתָּה, “cursed are you,” אָתָּה is the subject and refers to Cain. The predicate אָרוּר describes his condition.
analysis.morphology: Independent personal pronoun, second person masculine singular, in the pausal form אָתָּה.
analysis.sense: you (are): the one addressed named or identified

analysis.evidence: מִן הָאֲדָמָה names the ground from which the curse separates Cain. The ground that received his brother’s blood will no longer yield its strength to him (4:12), and Cain describes the sentence as expulsion from the ground (4:14).
analysis.morphology: Independent preposition without a prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The relative clause אֲשֶׁר פָּצְתָה אֶת פִּיהָ personifies the ground beneath Abel as opening its mouth to receive his blood. The feminine singular verb פָּצְתָה agrees with הָאֲדָמָה.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute common noun with the definite article הָ־.
analysis.sense: the ground underfoot; the face of the earth

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces the clause describing הָאֲדָמָה, “the ground which opened its mouth.” The feminine singular verb פָּצְתָה agrees with הָאֲדָמָה, and the suffix on פִּיהָ refers to the ground.
analysis.morphology: Invariable relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In the relative clause introduced by אֲשֶׁר, the feminine singular verb agrees with הָאֲדָמָה, “the ground.” Its direct object is אֶת־פִּיהָ, “its mouth.” The ground is personified as opening its mouth to receive the blood of Cain’s brother.
analysis.sense: to open wide, said of the mouth

analysis.evidence: In פָּצְתָה אֶת פִּיהָ, “it opened its mouth,” אֶת marks פִּיהָ as the direct object of פָּצְתָה. The possessive suffix ־הָ refers to הָאֲדָמָה, “the ground,” and makes “its mouth” definite.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object marker, unsuffixed, with no prefix.

analysis.evidence: The ground opened its mouth (פָּצְתָה אֶת־פִּיהָ) to receive the brother’s blood (אֶת־דְּמֵי אָחִיךָ) from Cain’s hand (מִיָּדֶךָ). The open mouth depicts the ground taking the blood into itself.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct with prefixed לְ (surfaced as לָ), expressing purpose

analysis.evidence: In לָקַחַת אֶת דְּמֵי אָחִיךָ, “to receive your brother’s blood,” אֶת marks דְּמֵי אָחִיךָ as the object of לָקַחַת. The possessive suffix on אָחִיךָ makes the construct phrase definite.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle, uninflected, without prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add Genesis 4:11 as evidence for the existing bloodshed sense of דָּם.
draft.definition: Blood shed in a killing, which can bear witness against the killer.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 4:11 the ground receives Abel’s blood from Cain’s hand.

analysis.evidence: דְּמֵי אָחִיךָ means “your brother’s shed blood.” The ground opens its mouth to receive that blood, and מִיָּדֶךָ, “from your hand,” identifies Cain as responsible for shedding it.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural construct noun, with no prefix or suffix. אָחִיךָ completes the construct phrase.
analysis.sense: bloodshed and responsibility for a death

analysis.evidence: In דְּמֵי אָחִיךָ, “your brother’s blood,” the suffix addresses Cain, and “brother” identifies Abel.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with a second-person masculine singular possessive suffix.

draft.change: Add Gen.4.11 as an example of the Hebrew hand-limb sense in yad.
draft.definition: The hand with which a person acts.
draft.evidence: In Gen.4.11 the ground receives Abel’s blood ‘from your hand’, addressing Cain.

analysis.evidence: The ground opens its mouth לָקַחַת אֶת דְּמֵי אָחִיךָ, ‘to receive your brother’s blood’. מִיָּדֶךָ identifies Cain’s hand as the source from which the ground receives the blood, pointing to Cain as the one who shed it.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed מִן ‘from’, with its נ assimilated to the doubled י, followed by the singular construct noun יָד and the second-person masculine singular possessive suffix ךָ ‘your’.
